scope: v1, 2 warmup + 5 measured, four streams, 4 MiB per stream, userspace UDP payload boundary, timings unusable by design
conclusions: Packet fill is no longer the deficit: netz averages 1,189-1,190 UDP payload bytes versus quic-go's 1,186-1,187 at this userspace boundary.
Netz still sends 3.33-4.26% more datagrams and 3.67-4.43% more bytes than quic-go in the matched roles.

Structured drop attribution again matches netz losses to quic-go dos_prevention drops (4081 vs 4102 upload, 3306 vs 3315 download); duplicate, payload-decrypt and other quic-go drop categories are zero.

The residual cost therefore remains the peer's bounded unprocessed-packet queue under this zero-latency workload, not malformed netz packets; this run does not claim encrypted-frame or kernel-wire equivalence.
